extracted.intended_audience: applicants and patent attorneys preparing and prosecuting Eurasian patent applications (EAPO)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural/substantive requirements for drafting, filing, examination, grant, opposition, enforcement and post-grant matters before the Eurasian Patent Office (EAPO). Intended to guide applicants and their representatives in meeting formal and substantive standards for Eurasian patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit of microorganisms (Budapest Treaty)
rubrics_metrics.description: For microorganisms the application must contain evidence of the depositing of the strain with an International Depositary Authority under the Budapest Treaty; the Administrative Council of the Eurasian Patent Organization may recognize other depositary institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Part II for institutions having status of International Depositary Authority. Evidence of deposit must be included in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listings for nucleotide/amino acid sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Eurasian patent application contains a sequence of nucleotides and/or amino acids, the specification should also contain this sequence provided on a machine-readable media according to the prescribed procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the prescribed procedure for machine-readable sequence submissions (format and media requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims: general requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims must define the subject matter for which protection is sought. The claims must be clear and concise and must be fully supported by the specification. The number of claims must be reasonable taking into consideration the nature of the invention claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should not be vague or unsupported; balance claim scope and number with nature of invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims: numbering and sentence structure
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is more than one claim, the claims must be numbered consecutively by Arabic numerals. Each claim must consist of one sentence, generally comprising an introductory (pre-characterizing) part and a characterizing part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use one-sentence claims with an introductory part (features common with closest prior art) and a characterizing part (preceded by 'characterized in that', 'characterized by', 'wherein the improvement comprises' or the like).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims: two-part format and wording
rubrics_metrics.description: In the introductory part, the technical features of the invention that are in common with the closest prior art shall be given including the generic concept reflecting the intended purpose of the invention. In the characterizing part ... the technical features distinguishing the claimed invention from the closest prior art shall be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede the characterising part with specified phrases ('characterized in that', etc.). Two-part form preferred except in certain cases (see exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims: permitted exceptions to two-part form
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may be drafted without separation into two parts if they characterize individual chemical compositions; strains of microorganisms, or culture cells of plants and animals; the use for a new purpose of an apparatus, method, substance or strain already known; or an invention for which there are no prior art solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use single-part claims in these special circumstances where the two-part format is inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims: avoid cross-reference to specification/drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall not (except if absolutely necessary) refer to the specification or drawings, e.g., in a manner like 'as described in part… of the specification', or 'as illustrated in figure…of the drawings'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on references to the description or drawings to define claim scope; claims should be self-contained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims: reference signs in claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application contains drawings, the technical features mentioned in the claims must preferably be followed by reference signs in brackets relating to such features if that provides for better understanding of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference signs are optional but recommended when they improve clarity; ensure consistency with drawing numerals mentioned in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent claims: single invention requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An independent claim must relate to one invention only. An application may contain two or more independent claims of the same category ... if it cannot be readily covered by a single general claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid drafting independent claims that claim multiple, unrelated inventions; multiple independent claims allowed when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claims: purpose and grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: A dependent claim must specify the features which constitute development or precise the features of the invention of the corresponding independent claim thus defining the invention in particular implementations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group all dependent claims relating to the same preceding independent claim together. Dependent claims may disclose specific features that could themselves be independent inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple dependency of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple dependency of claims is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft multiple-dependent claims where appropriate, subject to formal requirements and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims fees: additional claims fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional claims fees are due for each claim exceeding five claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget for fees if claiming more than five claims; check fee schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract: length and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract must be as concise as the disclosure allows, and should not exceed 150 words. The abstract must contain a summary of the disclosure contained in the description, claims and drawings. This summary must specify the technical field ... and the gist of the invention mentioning the technical result obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract is for technical information only and is not to be used for interpreting scope of protection. Include the most representative chemical formula if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract: drawings and reference numerals
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract must be accompanied by at least one drawing. Each essential feature contained in the abstract and illustrated by the drawing must be accompanied by a reference numeral in brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include at least one drawing linked to the abstract and use reference numerals for essential features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings: medium, style and legibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawings must be made in black, indelible, well-defined lines and strokes without colouring or shading on sheets of strong, white, smooth, non-shiny and durable paper of A4 international size. The scale and clarity of the drawings must be such that all details can be distinguished without difficulty after linear reduction in size to two-thirds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure high contrast, clear line work and that reduction to two-thirds still leaves all details legible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings: numerals, letters and prohibited elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Brackets, circles or inverted commas may not be used in association with numbers and letters. Numbers and letters in the drawings must be at least 3.2 mm high. The drawings may not contain text matter, except, where this is indispensable, for a single word or words such as 'water', 'steam', 'open', 'closed', 'section on AB', or the like. No dimensions are to be given in the drawings; where necessary, the dimensions must be given in the specification. Reference numerals not mentioned in the specification shall not appear in the drawings, and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep drawings free of excessive text and ensure consistency between drawings and specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory material other than drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanatory material other than drawings must be presented in the form of graphic material (e.g., diagrams, graphs, blueprints, sketches, oscillograms, etc.), photographs, tables or diagrams. Sketches can be submitted only if it is impossible to illustrate the specification by drawings or diagrams. Photographs can be submitted only to complement other graphic material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use photographs sparingly and only as complements; prefer drawings/diagrams for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic material numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: The graphic material must be numbered in Arabic numerals corresponding to those in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistent Arabic numeral numbering across specification and graphic material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of unitary procedural fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The required fees are the unitary procedural fee for filing, novelty search, publication of application and others (no separate filing fee is provided). The document configuring payment of the unitary procedural fee shall be submitted at the same time as the Eurasian application. This document may, together with proof of payment of the required surcharge of 20%, still be submitted within two months from filing. If said document is not filed in time, the application will be considered withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely file proof of payment or use the two-month grace period with 20% surcharge; otherwise application deemed withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment time limit for applications filed via National Patent Office
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of a Eurasian application from a Contracting State which is filed with the National Patent Office ... the time limit for filing the proof of payment of the unitary procedural fee is three months from mailing to the applicant a notification by the National Patent Office regarding transmittal of the Eurasian application to the Eurasian Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the three-month rule when filing via National Patent Office; ensure payment to avoid transmission/withdrawal issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant time limits and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limits allowed to applicant by the Eurasian Patent Office may not be less than two months and not be more than four months. In individual cases, the time limits may be extended upon request made before their expiration or within two months after their expiration together with payment of the required extension fee for each month of extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request extensions before expiry or within two months after with extension fees per month; observe minimum/maximum two-to-four-month terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing Authority and online filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent authority of the Eurasian Patent Organization is the Eurasian Patent Office located in Moscow. Online filing of Eurasian applications is possible for Eurasian patent attorneys through the ADEPT EAPO system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ADEPT EAPO for online filings when represented by an authorized Eurasian patent attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal examination: timing and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eurasian Patent Office examines the application for its correspondence to the formal requirements within two months from the filing date ... During the formal examination, it will be examined whether all required documents have been filed and are in compliance with the requirements, whether the invention is correctly classified according to the IPC, whether the priority claim(s) made (if any) is (are) statutory and whether or not the invention relates to subject matter which is unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may invite applicant to correct/amend within a prescribed term; formal examination period extends correspondingly if invitations issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search: automatic novelty search and basis
rubrics_metrics.description: A novelty search is carried out automatically for each Eurasian patent application that has been accepted for further prosecution. The search is to be carried out on the basis of the claims, taking into consideration the specification and drawings (if any).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claims and specification clearly disclose the invention as search is claim-focused. Search performed by Rospatent under agreement with EAPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search: handling lack of unity
rubrics_metrics.description: If during the patent search it is revealed that the requirement of unity of invention is not met, the applicant may be invited within three months from sending of the notification to communicate a decision which invention(s) shall be searched. If the applicant has not replied in time ... the search is carried out in respect of the invention mentioned first in the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize claims order or respond timely to unity notifications to control search scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search: sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The search is mainly carried out on the basis of the following sources ... (lists major patent offices, EPO, WIPO, national patent docs, international scientific/technical publications for at least five years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect broad international prior art searching including EPO/WIPO and major national patents; copies of cited documents can be provided upon request and payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to submit prior art/corresponding searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are not required to submit prior art or foreign search results or corresponding application numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination: request and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: All Eurasian patent applications are subject to substantive examination ... The substantive examination does not start automatically but is triggered by a request of the applicant. The examination request must be made and the examination fee paid before expiration of six months from the date of publication of the search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the search report and application are published together, count six months from publication of the application; late requests possible within two months with legitimate reasons and additional fee; otherwise the application is considered withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination: office actions and replies
rubrics_metrics.description: During substantive examination, the applicant may receive Office actions. An issued Office action shall be responded to within four months from the date of its sending; this term may be extended upon request and payment of a fee ... If a term for responding to an Office action is not observed, the application shall be considered withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond timely or request extensions with fees; if copies of cited documents are requested within three months, the reply term starts from sending those copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination ends by issuance of a decision on grant of the patent or on refusal of patent grant, based on the results of the substantive examination and made by a board of three examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board of three examiners issues the final substantive decision; plan prosecution accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination / grant options
rubrics_metrics.description: At the applicant’s request and subject to the payment of a fee, the Eurasian Patent Office conducts: accelerated formal examination within five days or within ten days; accelerated substantive examination (first office action will be issued within three months); accelerated publication and grant of a Eurasian patent (within fourteen days after the grant decision or the request for acceleration, whichever period expires later).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request and pay for acceleration where speed is critical; check fee schedule and procedural prerequisites.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH / PCT-PPH conditions for accelerated substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant of a PCT application entering Eurasian regional phase can request accelerated substantive examination provided that in respect of the corresponding PCT application it was determined by one of certain ISAs/IPEAs that at least one independent claim meets patentability requirements, and the claims in the Eurasian application are sufficiently in conformity with one or more said claims determined as patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure conformity with claims found patentable by specified ISAs/IPEAs (EPO, JPO, KIPO, Rospatent, USPTO) to qualify for accelerated examination under PCT-PPH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments during pendency and added subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may amend the claims during the whole time of application pendency before receiving the Decision on Patent Grant or on Refusal of Patent Grant. Any amendments or additional materials which modify the subject matter of the claimed invention disclosed in the application (i.e., containing features for including into the claims but absent in the application as filed originally) shall not be taken into consideration for the examination of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend freely before decision but avoid adding new matter; added subject-matter will be disregarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections of clerical/obvious errors in granted patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may request the Eurasian Patent Office to correct clerical or obvious errors in a granted Eurasian patent. If the error is attributable to the applicant, a fee must be paid. Information on the corrections made in a Eurasian patent is published in the Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use correction procedure for clerical mistakes; pay fees if applicant-caused; corrections are published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Not applicable in this jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EAPO does not provide for third party observations in its procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant: Notification on Readiness to Grant and payment
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is found that a patent may be granted, the applicant is notified by an intermediate document ... the fees for grant and publication of grant shall be paid within four months from the date of sending of this Notification. Instead of paying the grant fees, the applicant within the same four-month term can submit further amendments and then the examination shall be continued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay grant/publication fees timely or submit further amendments within four months; failure to act results in deemed withdrawal (with limited late payment options and surcharges).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant: publication, registration and scope across Contracting States
rubrics_metrics.description: If the grant fees are paid in time the patent will be granted and registered in the Register of Eurasian Patents, and a patent certificate will be issued ... The application for the grant of a Eurasian patent automatically covers all the Contracting States, and the Eurasian patent is granted with respect to all these States. After grant, no validation or registration of the Eurasian patent in the Contracting States is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eurasian patent is unitary across Contracting States; translations generally not required for the Contracting States, but national courts may require translations in proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition-after-grant (Administrative Revocation): time limit and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: During a period of six months from the publication of the particulars of the granted Eurasian patent in the Gazette, any person other than the patentee may file ... a Notice of Opposition against the grant of the patent. In opposition proceedings, the patent may be considered partly or totally invalid on the ground that the invention does not meet the conditions of patentability, or on the ground that the claims of the patent contain features which were absent in the application materials as originally filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition must contain explanations and is accompanied by a fee. Regulations prescribe that the Notice shall be considered within six months from receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition outcomes and amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Administrative Revocation procedure on opposition, the Eurasian Patent Office may decide to revoke the patent, to allow amending or correcting the patent, or to reject the Notice of Opposition. If the Office proposes an amendment ... the Office will decide to maintain the patent as amended if the owner agrees and pays the required fee for publication of the new specification within the prescribed term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amendments are accepted and publication fees paid, the patent is maintained as amended; failure to pay required fees can cause revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-examination availability
rubrics_metrics.description: A re-examination procedure is not available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No separate re-examination route exists in EAPO procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal: timing, composition and finality
rubrics_metrics.description: If the grant of a patent is refused, the applicant may, within three months from the date of sending of the notice of refusal, lodge an appeal ... The appeals are examined by a Board of three examiners, at least two not having been involved in taking of the decision which is appealed. The appeal should be considered within four months ... The decision on the appeal is final if it is approved by the President of the Eurasian Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File appeals timely with required fee; expect Board review within approx. four months; Presidential approval makes decision final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention (formal unity requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application may relate only to one invention or to a group of inventions so linked as to form a single general inventive concept. If the unity requirement is not met, the applicant must restrict the application to an invention or group of inventions meeting this requirement, and for the other inventions divisional application(s) may be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claims present a single inventive concept or be prepared to file divisionals for unrelated inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional applications: filing timing and examination fees
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application shall be filed before issuance of the Decision on Patent Grant or until expiration of the term for lodging appeal against the refusal decision. The examination request must be made and the examination fee paid before expiration of six months from the date of publication of the search report. Where the search report under the parent application can be used for the examination of the divisional application, the fee for substantive examination of the divisional application shall be paid within six months from the date of publication of the search report under the parent application. If six months have expired at the time of filing the divisional application, the fee for the substantive examination should be paid on the filing date of the divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File divisionals within permitted window and pay examination fees timely; use parent search report where applicable to save cost/time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuation applications are not applicable in this jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect a US-style continuation procedure in EAPO practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion to national applications after refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: If the grant of a Eurasian patent is refused, the applicant may convert the application into one or more national application(s) in the Contracting States ... The request may be filed until expiration of six months from the notice of refusal to grant a Eurasian patent or (if appeal has been lodged) the notice of refusal to allow the appeal. A fee must be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion preserves the filing and priority dates; EAPO forwards certified copy to designated national offices after fee payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eurasian patent application is published together with the search report as soon as possible after expiration of eighteen months from the filing date or ... from the priority date. The publication includes: the front page; the abstract; the description; the claims; the drawings and other material; and the search report (if available). The applicant may request publication at any time before expiration of the eighteen-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early publication triggers provisional protection; if search report is published separately it will be accompanied by the front page and abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access prior to publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to publication, the application will be accessible to third parties only if requested or authorized by the applicant or if requested by a court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control pre-publication access by request/authorization; otherwise applications remain confidential until publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal to prevent publication
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is withdrawn or considered withdrawn or refused no later than two months before the intended date of its publication, the application shall not be published; ... the application shall be withdrawn at least two months before the intended date of publication, i.e., within sixteen months after the filing date or priority date, if priority is claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid publication, withdraw at or before 16 months from filing/priority (two months before 18-month publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nullity and revocation grounds and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: A Eurasian patent may in each of the Contracting States be nullified ... if the invention does not meet the conditions of patentability, if the claims contain features absent in the application as originally filed, or in case of incorrect indication of the inventor or the owner. The national courts ... must apply the Eurasian Patent Convention and Regulations under it. Nullification is effective only in the territory of the State(s) where the nullification decision has been made. Partial nullification is possible if allowed by the national legislation. Nullification has retroactive effect as from the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nullity decisions are national in effect though based on EAPC; expect retroactive effect to filing date; partial nullification possible depending on national law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrender of patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner of a Eurasian patent may surrender the patent in respect of any of the Contracting States in which it is effective, by filing a written declaration to that effect with the Eurasian patent office and paying the required fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surrender can be limited to particular Contracting States; file written declaration and pay fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working/use requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no provisions on working in the Eurasian patent law. The working requirements will be based in each Contracting State where the Eurasian patent is valid on the provisions of the national law of that State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check national laws of individual Contracting States for working/compulsory licensing implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking of patented products
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no provisions in the Eurasian patent law on marking of patent protected products, and marked products have no implications for awarding compensation in case of past infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marking is governed by national law; do not rely on EAPO marking provisions for compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of protection and claim interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of protection provided by a Eurasian patent is determined by the claims. The specification and drawings serve merely to interpret the claims. When interpreting the claims, due account is to be taken of every feature of the invention contained in an independent claim or a feature being equivalent thereto. The doctrine of equivalents can be used when the legislation of the Contracting State allows its applying. The interpretation of claims should serve not only to clarify the features thereof which are unclear or indefinite, but also to determine their complete and actual scope; when interpreting the claims the extremes of a strict, literal interpretation ... and a broad interpretation ... must be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation should balance literal wording and specification to determine actual scope; national courts may apply doctrine of equivalents subject to national law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringing acts: product and method claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The following acts done without the consent of the owner of a patent are deemed patent infringement: – in the case of a patent for a product – the manufacture, use, importation, offering for sale, sale or any other kind of marketing or the storage for that purpose, of the product; – in the case of a patent for a method – the use of that method or the offering of that method for use, and ... the use, importation, offering for sale, sale or any other kind of marketing or storage for that purpose of a product directly obtained by the patented method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method patent protection extends to products directly obtained by the patented method until rebutted by proof to the contrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect (contributory) infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: At present, there are no provisions in the Eurasian patent law on indirect (contributory) infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect an express contributory infringement cause of action under EAPO law; rely on national law where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-infringing acts / exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The following are not deemed infringement: – use for scientific and experimental purposes; – use for private non-commercial purposes only; – use in construction/operation of means of transport of certain States temporarily entering territory; – extemporaneous preparation of a medicine in a pharmacy on prescription; – acts regarding a product after it has been put on the market in that State by the owner (exhaustion). Use of a patented drug for experimental purposes, including clinical experiments and trials, is also not deemed infringement ('Bolar provision').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory exceptions limit infringement actions; consider them in litigation and enforcement contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior user rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who before the filing date ... has in good faith used a solution identical to the patented invention on the territory of a Contracting State ... may continue that use or start that use free of charge, provided that the scope of the use is not expanded. Such right may be transferred only together with the production unit in which the use is made ... The prior user's right exists only in the Contracting State(s) in which the prior use has occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior users have a territorial, non-expandable, potentially transferable (with production unit) right; check evidence of prior use and territory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies and licensee participation
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of infringement, the following remedies are available: injunction; award of damages; compensation for moral damage; and any other remedies as provided by the legislation of the Contracting State concerned. Any licensee may take part in infringement proceedings before the court instituted by the patent owner, ... An exclusive licensee may bring an infringement action on own initiative, except if provided otherwise in the licence contract. Any licensee may bring an infringement action in his own name if the patent owner ... does not take action within one month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies vary by national law; licensees have procedural rights to protect their interests, including bringing suits under certain conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation period for infringement claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The ultimate term for infringement action is three years after the date on which plaintiff became aware or should have become aware of the infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor discovery/knowledge dates to preserve claims; national limitation rules may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of published application (provisional protection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional protection starts from the date of publication of the application. After publication of the Eurasian patent, the patent owner may claim ... a reasonable compensation ... from the persons who without the owner's consent used the invention ... during the period from the date of publication of the application until the date of publication of the Eurasian patent. The provisional protection is limited to the scope of the published claims of the application. For PCT applications designating EAPO provisional protection starts on the date of publication of the international application if the application is published in Russian; otherwise only after submitting a translation into Russian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional protection is limited and conditional; if grant is finally refused, provisional protection is considered never to have existed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penal provisions, enforcement and customs
rubrics_metrics.description: See the respective country chapters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal/administrative enforcement and customs measures are addressed at the national level in country-specific chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration after unintentional lapse
rubrics_metrics.description: Restoration shall be effected in relation to one or more Contracting States on the territory of which the Eurasian patent was valid, and the legislation of which provides for the restoration of the right to a patent. Restoration of right to a patent is currently provided for in all EAPO Contracting Parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration is governed by national law and can be effected where national legislation permits; check domestic rules and procedures.
